heading: January 2025 expansion plans
body:
On January 15, 2025, President-elect Donald Trump said he would use the momentum of the newly agreed Gaza ceasefire deal to expand the Abraham Accords, the US-backed agreements struck during his first term that normalized Israel's relations with several Arab countries.[n] Writing on Truth Social, Trump said his national security team, through Special Envoy to the Middle East [[steve-witkoff|Steve Witkoff]], would continue working closely with Israel and allies to ensure Gaza never again became a terrorist safe haven, and would keep "promoting PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH throughout the region, as we build upon the momentum of this ceasefire to further expand the Historic Abraham Accords."[n]

Badlands contributor GhostofBasedPatrickHenry offered a speculative reading of the Accords as a diplomatic weapon: not, as marketed to the American public, an instrument to protect Israel from the Arabs, but a mechanism designed to protect the Arabs from what he called the "evil twin" in Tel Aviv by exposing and destroying it.[n] He noted that when the Emiratis and [[jared-kushner|Jared Kushner]] assembled the Accords they intentionally left out Saudi Arabia and Palestine, and that the moment they were signed on September 15, 2020, Saudi Crown Prince [[mohammed-bin-salman|Mohammed bin Salman]] dispatched the recently promoted Foreign Minister [[faisal-bin-farhan|Faisal bin Farhan]] to begin work on an Israel–Saudi normalization deal that would fold Saudi Arabia into the Accords and represent a symbolic peace between Israel and Islam.[n] In that framing, the prospect of a genuine regional stabilization — which would render future plans for the [[greater-israel-project|Greater Israel Project]] all but impossible — is why the [[october-7-attacks|October 7th attacks]] happened, with Trump "chumming the waters" via the Accords and MBS "poking the sharks" with the normalization track.[n]

heading: Abraham Accords and the 2025 ceasefire framing
body: Badlands commentary in January 2025 argued that a genuine Israeli–Saudi normalization deal, folding Saudi Arabia into the [[abraham-accords|Abraham Accords]], would stabilize the region enough to make future plans regarding the Greater Israel Project "all but impossible" — and identified that prospect as the motive behind the [[october-7-attacks|October 7th attacks]].[n] Separately, contributor Burning Bright wrote that by advancing a Gaza peace deal Donald Trump had placed the [[israel-lobby|Israel lobby]] in a position where any overt move to restart kinetic action would be seen for what it was: an attempt to escalate and progress toward the Greater Israel Project.[n] If Israel declined the chance at peace, the argument ran, Trump would hold a bipartisan public mandate to break with it on a level never seen before.[n]

heading: Trump and the Middle East (2025)
body:
In a January 2025 Badlands News Brief essay, contributor Burning Bright described the Middle East as the Kobayashi Maru of both the Info War and the Shadow War, translated to the masses through what he termed the War of Stories.[n] He observed that [[elon-musk|Elon Musk]] had begun routinely invoking the refrain to describe the position of the sociopolitical establishment as the Trump era rose to new heights.[n] Recounting the fictional Star Trek test in which prospective Starfleet captains face an impossible scenario, he emphasized that James T. Kirk refused to accept its parameters — which he judged nihilist and defeatist — and reprogrammed the simulation with new victory conditions, rescuing the stranded starship while keeping his own crew alive.[n]

On that reading, Donald Trump is "the James T. Kirk of the Info War and the Shadow War," and his Kobayashi Maru is the Middle East.[n] Burning Bright tied this to the "Saving Israel for last" comms threaded through the Q drops, argued that Trump's Gaza peace-deal narrative had placed several establishment factions into their own versions of the impossible test, and concluded that "from the Doha Agreement to the Abraham Accords to 'not so Greater' Israel, Trump isn't merely solving the Kobayashi Maru ... he IS the Kobayashi Maru."[n]
